summary: First backend test run for CONEXIA CLM MVP. All 18 pytest cases passed (100%). Covered: health, idempotent /api/seed (5 contracts), dev-login + /auth/me (valid/invalid/missing tokens), dashboard KPIs+alerts+recent, contracts list/filter/get/create with persistence verification, full 4-step workflow approval rollup to 'approved', mock e-sign with audit hash, addenda creation (parent_contract_id, value rollup, parent timeline event), evidence creation with GPS/timestamp and contract timeline event, evidence list/get/filter, and AI /api/ai/analyze using Claude Sonnet via emergentintegrations returning valid JSON schema (summary, key_dates, financial_obligations, risk_clauses, overall_risk). No critical or minor backend issues found. The seed user demo@conexia.io is created during /api/seed and via /api/auth/dev-login (no shared password - dev-login bypass is the intended demo entry).

minor.issue: Filter matches the DB-stored status field, but compute_status() can override the returned status on read (e.g. an 'active' contract within 30 days of end_date is reported as 'expiring' in the response). Result is consistent for the seed but UI may see items whose returned status != requested filter. Consider applying compute_status before filtering, or document this behavior.
Sign endpoint does not validate that workflow is fully approved before signing. Any authenticated user can sign a draft contract. Acceptable for MVP/demo but worth gating in production.
Uses query parameter (email: str = 'demo@conexia.io') as a default. Functions correctly but unusual - consider a Pydantic body for consistency with the rest of the API.

action_items: (Optional) Decide whether GET /api/contracts?status=active should apply compute_status() before filtering so the returned list always matches the filter.
(Optional) Gate POST /contracts/{id}/sign behind workflow status == 'approved' for production builds.
Frontend tests are still pending (per request, this iteration was backend-only).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~830 lines and still single-file; acceptable for MVP but consider splitting into routers/services as the codebase grows beyond 1k lines.
All datetimes are returned ISO-8601 UTC via doc_clean(); _id is correctly excluded everywhere.
AI call uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 via emergentintegrations (anthropic provider) with a strict JSON system prompt and a regex fallback parser - robust.
Indexes are created on startup (users.email/user_id unique, sessions.session_token unique, TTL on expires_at, contracts.contract_id unique, evidence.evidence_id unique). Good.
CORS is wide-open (allow_origins=['*']) - acceptable for preview, tighten for production.
seed_data_creation: Used existing POST /api/seed to populate 5 demo contracts and the demo@conexia.io user. Tests also create TEST_-prefixed contracts/evidence (not cleaned up - acceptable for demo DB).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green. For the next iteration, run frontend tests on Expo web preview at https://contract-forge-35.preview.emergentagent.com. Use POST /api/auth/dev-login to bootstrap session_token (token starts with 'dev_'). Demo user: demo@conexia.io / role=direction. The single test file /app/backend/tests/test_conexia_clm.py can be re-run as regression. AI test waits up to 90s for Claude Sonnet response.
